children: Bitcoin exchange-traded funds traded more than $7.5 billion in the week ending October 16, 2026. Investors still pulled out roughly $145 million on net over the same stretch.
Cumulative trading volume across the US spot Bitcoin ETFs topped $7.5 billion through October 16. Several sessions in the period cleared $2 billion in trading value.
The standout day was October 8, when trading hit $3.18 billion. October 14 was also heavy, with $2.29 billion in trading value.
Despite all that activity, the funds recorded approximately $145 million in net outflows for the week. A separate five-day tally put the net outflow at $125.1 million.
The weekly outflow fits into a bigger October pattern. Month-to-date outflows have reached approximately $535 million.
Much of that came from one bruising session. On October 7, the funds saw a $485 million single-day exit, which accounts for most of the month's damage so far.
September 2026 was largely marked by positive inflows, so October's reversal stands out by comparison.
Through all of it, Bitcoin itself held up. The price traded near $82,000 during the period of net redemptions.

The biggest names in the space drove much of the action. BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC, along with Grayscale's products, accounted for substantial trading activity and saw meaningful movement in both inflows and outflows.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024. Since then, cumulative net inflows have reached around $57 billion.

Total assets under management now sit between $105 billion and $106 billion. Against that backdrop, a $145 million weekly outflow is a rounding error, roughly a fraction of a percent of the asset base.
Even October's approximately $535 million in month-to-date outflows looks modest next to the $57 billion that has come in since launch.

Market observers noted that heavy volume paired with contained outflows may point to less selling from weaker hands. If nervous holders were rushing for the exits, the outflows would likely look far larger than $145 million on more than $7.5 billion in turnover.
The things to watch are fairly simple. First, whether daily flows turn positive again or keep trickling out through the rest of October.
Second, whether IBIT and FBTC, as the leading products, resume steady inflows. Third, whether Bitcoin can keep holding near $82,000 if outflows continue.

title: Bitcoin ETFs trade over $7.5B in a week despite $145M in net selling
